narrative:
The model predicts an 81% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart in the near future.

Three factors stood out most in driving this prediction. First, the model noticed that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is the strongest signal the system uses, and in your case it strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving. Second, your overall career experience of 6-10 years also increased the likelihood of departure. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (half have only 1-5 years), your level of experience pulled the prediction toward leaving. Third, your monthly salary in the 11k-15k SAR range contributed to the decision. This salary bracket is relatively uncommon among those expected to stay and worked against you by increasing the chance of leaving.

Taken together, these elements outweighed many positive aspects of your profile, such as receiving a bonus, feeling recognized, and reporting job stability.

The organization should discuss retention options with you, especially around competitive external offers and compensation alignment. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still matches your career goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook going forward. (218 words)
